Consider the rectangle $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 2}.
$$

The transformation $T$ is defined as

$$
x=2u-v+1,\,y=u-v+1.

activity_context.topic_title: The Image of an Affine Transformation

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Polygon Under an Affine Transformation
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/dd8b1407add93e72afccf2138cc818df63d47fdaa6ccc23e843a5602d8c1dbd8.png)

          

Consider the rectangle $\Delta$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
\Delta  = \big\{ (u,v) \: : \: -1 \leq u \leq 1, \: -1\leq v \leq 1 \big\}.
$$

The transformation $\mathbf T$ is defined as

$$
x = u - v + 1, \qquad y = u+v
$$

Find the image of $\Delta$ in the $xy$-plane under the action of $\mathbf T.$
examples.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $\mathbf T:\mathbb R^2\rightarrow\mathbb R^2$ is a function of the form

$$
\mathbf x = A \mathbf u + \mathbf b,
$$

where $\mathbf x, \mathbf u,$ and $\mathbf b$ are column vectors in $\mathbb R^2,$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that we can express the given transformation as 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u-v+1 \\ u+v\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u-v \\ u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $\mathbf T$ maps the boundary of $\Delta$ to the boundary of the image. So, to find the image of $\Delta,$ we find the images of each side.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/69d92e24d5b0c81e54d3878793efe7c07d16fc963222997fe4fec4ffb3f93bd5.png)

          

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing all vertices of our square:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/047cd6bf2960418919b4a11ae6920d9fc589881062ddbb3eed918116a7e4c4fd.png)

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $\mathbf b$ in each column:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/cfc1c3e72dd7764d9835e35f1943ef96c6829703ca8f0b2bce67153df9df88e5.png)

The image of $\mathbf u$ under $T$ is given by $A\mathbf u + \mathbf b.$ So, by applying $\mathbf T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & -1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ -2 & 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertices of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(1,-2), (3,0), (1,2),$ and $(-1,0).$

Drawing this region in the $xy$-plane, we get the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/ddd14bdebe21c830396e044721811cf6b9c7bd7db067e4d0ff7d35e02a592894.png)

          

Notice that since $\det(A) = 2 >    0,$ this transformation is orientation-preserving.

feedback.problem:
Consider the transformation $T$ defined as

$$
x=v-2u-3,\,y=u+v+3.
$$

Let $P(1,1)$ be a point in the $uv$-plane. Suppose that the image of $P$ under the action of $T$ is the point ${P}^{′}$ in the $xy$-plane. What are the coordinates of ${P}^{′}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}v-2u-3 \\ u+v+3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2u+v \\ u+v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the image of $P$ under the action of $T,$ we first create a column vector $u$ containing the coordinates of $P:$

$$
u=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Applying $T$ to $u,$ we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of ${P}^{′}$ are $(-4,5).$
